newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks security pact with NATO candidates.
newsitem.headline: France seeks security pact with NATO candidates.

text.p: France wants to build a security partnership with NATO candidate countries not invited to join the alliance in its first round of eastward expansion, a spokeswoman for President Jacques Chirac said on Monday.

"France wants the alliance to develop a security partnership with candidate states that would not be initially invited to negotiate their membership in the alliance," Catherine Colonna told reporters after a meeting between Chirac and Latvian President Guntis Ulmanis.
She said Chirac wanted the partnership to take the form of a charter between NATO and Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Finland and Sweden.
NATO members are set to meet in Madrid in July to begin the process of expanding the alliance eastward.
Former Communist Warsaw Pact members Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are likely to be invited to start talks about their membership.
France has tried to have Romania included in this first group of nations, but has encountered resistance from other NATO members.
Russia, which is opposed to NATO expansion, is in talks on an agreement establishing a new relationship with the alliance before giving its grudging approval to the move.
Last week, Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said President Boris Yeltsin would travel to Paris on May 27 to sign the accord if it was ready in time.
